why: OpenSandbox/Daytona ordinary command cancellation leaves escaped FD writers; SRT process wrapper lacks resource control and explicit old-wrapper revocation. Existing Docker/Linux topic compares actual namespace lifecycle and configured limits, not another required OSS project.
environment: Linux Docker Engine28.0.1 behind current WSL DockerDesktop; product target Linux Engine API, no Windows path or host bindings accepted.

cases.question: Can a known Linux ext4 fixture be bind-mounted, preserving host byte identity and uid1000 writes? Fail if daemon does not see source; no silent copy fallback for this property.

With read-only rootfs, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, network none and one RW domain: own writes succeed, other/host-canary/control-socket absent, symlink cannot reach host fixture; actual uid/capabilities/proc/net recorded.

Real setsid orphan child preopens RW FD; external driver records readiness then kills entire container by full ID, waits for actual exited status and process absence; trigger after stop must not write. Negative control same child before kill must write.

Actual cgroup files show memory128MiB, pids32 and cpu0.5 limits; bounded fork attempts <=48 hit EAGAIN and bounded memoryallocation<=192MiB produces OOM/rejection. These are exploratory probe limits, not final workload SLA.
Explicit upstream engine-version seccomp profile is applied and /proc/Seccomp confirms mode2; current daemon default unconfined does not count. Failure to load actual profile remains failure.

oracles: Host fixture bytes, real process and cgroup observations and Docker inspect state, not candidate success labels. Each container has unique lore-g2 label/name; keep raw create/inspect/log/wait/remove outputs.
stop: <=45sec each command; bounded<=8containers total and one concurrent, memory<=128MiB/cpu0.5/pids32/tmp16MiB; cleanup only exact created IDs in finally; no real credentials/network/provider calls or other user workloads touched.
limits: Same-kernel nonprivileged container threat scope; no kernel-escape/host-admin/Docker daemon compromise proof, no powerloss/crosshost recovery or storage quota claim. Config alone is not resource enforcement evidence.
